decision.title: The sxml command asks for no step bound (packet )
decision.summary: The sxml command sets maximum_evaluation_step_count to UINT64_MAX, so its runs have no step bound in practice, while embedders and the JavaScript package keep the library default.

item.p: Mechanism: the command's one processor configuration (apps/sxml/query_command.c, shared by xpath, xquery, transform, serialize, validate and check) sets sxml_processor_limits.maximum_evaluation_step_count to UINT64_MAX (SXML_QUERY_MAXIMUM_EVALUATION_STEP_COUNT). The header has no value for "no bound": 0 means the library's default of 10^8. The largest count is no bound in practice (about 585 years at a step a nanosecond), and the charge in sxml_dynamic_context_charge_steps cannot overflow at it. No named constant is proposed: the header's interface stays as it is (), and an embedder that wants no bound writes the same value.
Kept: the library's default for embedders and the JavaScript package; the conformance drivers' bounds (, ); entity expansion stays bounded to 4 MiB; a run is stopped with Ctrl-C.

Test: cli/xpath_no_step_limit, (1 to 20000) = (1 to 20000): a general comparison is charged a step per pair up front (), 4 x 10^8, and finds its match at once. It gave LIMIT_EXCEEDED (exit 4) before and gives true() now, in milliseconds under every preset; a loop of 10^8 real steps takes 25 s in a loaded release build and far longer under the sanitizers, so no test runs one.

Book: "The step limit" (performance.md) shows the command running past the default and says how to stop a run; appendix-differences.md, ixml-performance.md and javascript.md cite it; c.md still shows the default for a C program. docs/CLI.md has a "Limits" rule.
